title: Keep a connected family-kind definition anchor for every core domain artifact

facts.note: Anchor nodes live under src/atdd/planner/conventions/nodes/; any change in the planner conventions tree (nodes or relationship edges) can affect anchor existence, kind or connectedness.
Task mentions a core domain artifact, its definition, or the planner convention/relationship graph.

values: any planner convention node added, removed, renamed or re-kinded
any relationship edge added, removed or rewired
facts.note: Diff-level observer over planner convention nodes and relationship edges; any such change (including to non-core nodes) can orphan or remove an anchor.
Validator finding must be surfaced to the planner; it also reports pre-existing violations regardless of what the current change touched.

fires: Planner changes the kind of planner.feature.definition from family to rule or constraint.
Planner removes or rewires relationship edges (including edges whose other end is a non-core node) so that planner.wmbt.definition is no longer a source_ref or target_ref of any edge.
The validator reports that one of the seven core artifacts already lacks an anchor, has a non-family anchor, or has an orphan anchor, even if the current task did not cause it.
doesNotFire: Demanding a definition anchor for a convention that is not one of the seven core domain artifacts.
Work confined to coder or tester conventions while all seven planner anchors exist, are kind family, and are graph-connected.

given: Core domain artifacts: theme, train, interlocking, wagon, feature, wmbt, artifact.
when: You change planner convention nodes or relationship edges, or the anchor validator reports a finding.
then: Each core artifact must have a `planner.<artifact>.definition` node of kind family that is a source_ref or target_ref of at least one relationship edge; a missing, non-family or orphan anchor is refused.
prefer: Author a missing anchor as src/atdd/planner/conventions/nodes/planner.<artifact>.definition.convention.yaml with kind family, then wire at least one edge from it via `atdd author relationship`.
avoid: Making an anchor kind rule/constraint or binding a validator to it; it is transitively protected by the constraint/rule nodes it requires.
Creating the anchor but leaving it an orphan.
unless: Only the seven core domain artifacts must carry an anchor; other conventions are unaffected.
why: The anchor gives each core artifact a stable meaning without binding a validator; it must both exist (this rule) and be graph-connected (planner.relationship.no-orphan-nodes).
evidence: For each of theme, train, interlocking, wagon, feature, wmbt, artifact: planner.<artifact>.definition exists, has kind family, and appears as source_ref or target_ref of at least one edge in the relationship graph.
verifier_detail: Core artifact set (exactly seven): theme, train, interlocking, wagon, feature, wmbt, artifact. Expected node id: planner.<artifact>.definition.
Refuse when the node is missing, when its kind is not family, or when it is an orphan (not a source_ref/target_ref of any edge).

Term definition_anchor: a planner.<artifact>.definition node of kind family that gives a core domain artifact a stable meaning without binding a validator (an advisory semantic anchor). Term core_domain_artifact: one of the seven planner domain-decomposition artifacts — theme, train, interlocking, wagon, feature, wmbt, artifact.
Pairs with planner.relationship.no-orphan-nodes: the anchor must both EXIST (this rule) and be graph-connected (no-orphan).
The anchor binds no validator itself; it is transitively protected by the constraint/rule nodes it requires.
Do not require anchors for conventions outside the seven core artifacts (exception scope).
